## Claims
- [proved] **Indexed graded Nakayama minimality criterion.** Let \(A=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}A_d\) be a commutative unital \(\mathbb Z\)-algebra with \(1\in A_0\) and \(A_0=\mathbb Z\), and put \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\). Let \(J\subseteq A\) be a homogeneous ideal, and let \(g_1,\ldots,g_N\in J\) be homogeneous elements such that \(J=\sum_{i=1}^NAg_i\). If their images \(\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_N\) are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J/A_+J\), then, for every \(k\), \(\{g_i:i\ne k\}\) does not generate \(J\). Indeed, if \(J=\sum_{i\ne k}Ag_i\), then modulo \(A_+J\), every coefficient \(a\in A\) acts through its degree-zero component in \(A/A_+=A_0=\mathbb Z\). Hence \(J/A_+J\) would be \(\mathbb Z\)-spanned by \(\{\bar g_i:i\ne k\}\), contradicting that \(\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_N\) is a basis.
- [proved] The ideal hypothesis is used as follows: since \(J\) is an ideal, \(A_+J\subseteq J\); since \(J\) is homogeneous, \(J/A_+J\) inherits the grading. The irredundance conclusion itself only uses \(A_+J\subseteq J\), \(A/A_+\cong\mathbb Z\), and the asserted basis property.
- [proved] More generally, for a graded \(A\)-module \(M\) bounded below in degree and homogeneous elements \(g_1,\ldots,g_N\), if their images generate \(M/A_+M\) over \(\mathbb Z\), then they generate \(M\). This follows by induction on degree: an element of degree \(d\) differs from a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of the \(g_i\) by terms \(am\) with \(\deg a>0\) and \(\deg m<d\). For a homogeneous ideal \(J\subseteq A\) with \(A\) nonnegatively graded, bounded-below is automatic.

## Strategy
Apply the criterion with \(J=J_v\). Thus, an independently established isomorphism
\[
J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^N
\]
under which the chosen \(N\) generators map to the displayed basis proves that no generator can be deleted.

## Gaps
The required basis statement for a general \(J_v/A_+J_v\) is not proved here. No independent review record was supplied.

## Next
For each proposed family, verify integrally—not merely after tensoring with \(\mathbb Q\)—that its image is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J_v/A_+J_v\).
